novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that “SAEs recover distinct monosemantic features for harmful intent versus harmful topic” and that those intent features support a “precise, interpretable guardrail,” so its novelty route is a proposed intent–topic representational separation and measurement rather than a new SAE paradigm. The closest retrieved work is Understanding Refusal in Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders (2025), which already identifies causal refusal features and uses them for harmful-input classification, while CRaFT (2026) explicitly notes that activation-selected safety features capture “topic or lexical cues” rather than causal refusal mechanisms; searches around “sparse autoencoder harmful intent topic safety monitor,” “SAE refusal features benign harmful prompts over-refusal,” and “LLM activation intent versus topic guardrail” therefore locate nearly all constituent ideas, though not the exact controlled intent-versus-topic decomposition. Moving from that work to contrastively selecting SAE features that track malicious intent while controlling for sensitive topic is a non-trivial but natural adaptation of established feature-selection and safety-monitoring methods, not a new core interpretability mechanism, warranting standard novelty rather than high novelty.
